prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: checked baggage from acceptance/transfer induction through screening, sorting, reconciliation, staging and aircraft-loading handoff; subsequent airline loading excluded.
Baggage Control System (Velvet) coordinates status/routing/visibility using current flight/operating data; associates tag identifiers with passenger/flight records, checks flight acceptance availability/completeness, and compares transfer data with routing information. Concourse Zone Controller (Mosslight) coordinates local conveyance, produces Recovery Route Card, and grants induction permissive only when equipment status/restrictions permit. Flight Data Gateway supplies flight/routing records and sends Flight Cutoff Advisory. Advisory recipient unspecified.
Staff confirm airline-rule carriage eligibility and passenger/flight details before acceptance, then check dimensions/weight against conveyor limits. Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit captures identification, records/initiates accepted-bag processing, and sends Oversize Exception Ticket for size-envelope exceedance. Bag Tag Printer produces durable, uniquely identified tags per accepted bag. Missing/unreadable/conflicting acceptance data require holding for staff resolution before induction; oversized bags await staff-approved handling routes in designated holding.
Transfer Bag Feeder identifies/records inbound transfer arrivals and sends Late Transfer Bag Card. Staff verify legible identifiers and valid onward-flight records. Before induction, records must be valid, routes available, receiving equipment ready. Induction Tray Conveyor uses controlled feed points and maintains bag separation.
North Gate Scanner/South Gate Scanner screen; Image Resolution Desk supports operator image review; Secondary Inspection Chute routes additional examination. Explosives Response Team/Security Duty Manager coordinate escalated security disposition. Primary Crossbelt Sorter routes cleared bags; Bag Reconciliation Station verifies identity/status. East Make-Up Conveyor/West Make-Up Conveyor convey to loading; Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit stages departures. Outbound Load Control Desk confirms handoff readiness; Airline Ramp Coordinator coordinates acceptance.
Baggage Operations Supervisor oversees flow/interruption recovery with Security Duty Manager/Maintenance Technician. Defined interfaces exchange equipment status, identity, routing state/restrictions; staff resolve automation-unclearable conditions. Objectives: safe screening, accurate bag-flight association, predictable throughput, departure-cutoff delivery. No explicit modes.

New part:
S045: Interlocks stop feed movement when a jam, access-door opening, or loss of downstream readiness is detected.
S046: The North Gate Scanner reads the bag identifier as the bag enters the screening and sorting network.
S047: The North Gate Scanner is also known locally as Kestrel.
S048: The South Gate Scanner provides an independent read point for bags routed through its assigned entry path.
S049: The Primary Crossbelt Sorter receives inducted bags and directs them according to the active routing data.
S050: The Primary Crossbelt Sorter is also known locally as Juniper.
S051: When automated image review cannot resolve a bag image, staff at the Image Resolution Desk assess the available image and record a disposition.
S052: The Airline Ramp Coordinator sends a Carousel Release Slip when the outbound build is authorized.
S053: The Baggage Control System applies the approved screening profile to each bag using its tag data and the current operating configuration.
S054: The Induction Tray Conveyor presents bags to the screening equipment at a controlled spacing that supports reliable image capture.
S055: The Primary Crossbelt Sorter maintains bag identity and routes each bag according to the screening disposition available at the time of sorting.
S056: The North Gate Scanner and South Gate Scanner acquire screening images and return a disposition for each bag that passes through them.
S057: Screening equipment records image quality and alarm status so that an incomplete examination is not treated as a clear result.
S058: When automated image review cannot resolve a bag image, staff at the Image Resolution Desk assess the available image and record a disposition.
S059: The reviewer considers the full image, bag identification, and any system prompts before assigning a disposition.
S060: A bag remains under controlled routing while its image is awaiting review, and the system prevents it from entering an outbound make-up path prematurely.
S061: The South Gate Scanner produces a Manual Rescan Receipt when a manual rescan is required.
S062: A clear disposition permits normal routing only when the bag identity and screening record agree.
S063: An alarm, an unresolved image, or a missing screening record places the bag into an exception status for additional examination.
S064: The Baggage Control System routes exception-status bags to the Secondary Inspection Chute through a path that avoids normal outbound flows.
S065: The chute is monitored for occupancy so that a bag is not released into a blocked or unavailable inspection position.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
